chunks: And in the narration of Abū Baṣīr from him, peace be upon him:
"If you speak or turn your face away from the qiblah, then repeat the salat (prayer)."

key_terms.أَبِي بَصِيرٍ: Abū Baṣīr, the narrator transmitting this report
key_terms.الْقِبْلَةِ: the direction of prayer toward which one must face
key_terms.وَجْهَكَ: your face, meaning one’s direction of facing

ai.seo_question: Does speaking or turning away from the qiblah invalidate salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding actions that invalidate salat (prayer). It states that speaking during the prayer or turning one’s face away from the qiblah necessitates repeating the prayer.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1057 - In the narration of Abu Basir from Imam (as),
Imam (as) said: "If you speak or turn your face away from the qibla, then you should repeat the prayer."
